transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I just can’t stop fixating on how bad I look in every picture, and it’s starting to really interfere with my work and my social life. It's gotten so overwhelming lately that I feel like I can't even focus on my job anymore.

Do you also have repeated unwanted thoughts or rituals, like checking, washing, counting, or arranging things, that you feel driven to do to reduce anxiety? Or is it mainly a preoccupation with how you look in photos?

No, it's not really about washing or counting things—it's entirely focused on how I look. I feel driven to do things like taking dozens of selfies to check my angles, zooming in on pictures, and redoing my makeup and outfits over and over to hide my nose and skin. I also constantly find myself asking my roommate or mom for reassurance about whether I look weird.
Do you believe there is a real flaw in your appearance that others can see, or do you worry that your concern may be excessive or not fully accurate?

To me, the flaws feel completely real and obvious—all I see in photos is how huge and crooked my nose is and how uneven my skin looks. Even though my family and coworkers tell me I look fine and don't notice anything, I still can't stop zooming in and fixating on it. It leaves me feeling really stuck between what I see so clearly and what everyone else tells me.
When you think about your nose or skin, do you ever believe with complete certainty that there is a real defect, or do you recognize that this concern might be exaggerated or mainly in your mind?

When I'm looking at a photo, I honestly believe with complete certainty that the defects are real because they are just so obvious to me. It's incredibly hard to think it's all in my mind when I can see my crooked nose right there on the screen. Even if I try to tell myself it might be exaggerated, in those moments, it feels one hundred percent real.
Do you ever hear, see, or strongly believe things about your appearance that other people say are not true, such as being watched, talked about, or targeted because of your looks?

No, I don't feel like people are watching me, talking about me, or targeting me because of how I look. My focus is purely on how bad I think I look in photos and in the mirror, and even though my mom and roommate tell me they don't notice anything wrong, I still strongly believe my nose is huge and crooked and my skin is uneven.
Have you ever had other unusual beliefs, like being watched, followed, or harmed because of your appearance, or is the concern limited only to your looks and photos?
No, I have never believed that I was being watched, followed, or harmed in any way. My concerns are strictly limited to my physical appearance and how bad I look in photos.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, such as hearing or seeing things that others do not, or feeling that people are trying to harm or control you?
No, I have never experienced hearing or seeing things that others do not. I've also never felt like anyone was trying to harm or control me in any way.
Do you ever think there is a chance your concern about your appearance could be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain the defect is real even when others disagree?

I feel completely certain that the flaws are real, because when I look in the mirror or at photos, the crookedness of my nose and my uneven skin are just so glaringly obvious. Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers tell me I look fine and that they don't notice anything, I honestly can't believe they don't see it too.
Have you ever been able to consider that your appearance concerns might be a false belief or an exaggeration, or are you completely unable to doubt them even a little?
I'm not really sure. It feels so completely real to me when I look at photos that I haven't ever thought about it being a false belief or an exaggeration.
When you are not looking at photos or in the mirror, do you ever think there is a chance that your appearance concerns might be exaggerated or untrue, or do you stay completely convinced even then?
I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't really thought about it in those terms, because the worry about how I look is just always there in the back of my mind.

When you are not checking mirrors or photos, can you ever recognize that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or are you completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?
I'm not quite sure and I haven't really thought about it that way. But whenever I do look at myself, the flaws feel completely real and it's just very distressing.

When you are not looking in mirrors or photos, can you ever think that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or are you completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?

I'm still not really sure how to answer that, because I haven't really thought about whether my concerns are exaggerated when I'm not looking at a screen or mirror. I just know that whenever I do see myself, it feels incredibly real and distressing.
Outside of looking in mirrors or photos, can you ever recognize that your concern about your appearance might be exaggerated, or do you stay completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?

It honestly feels completely real to me all the time, and I find it hard to believe otherwise. Even though others try to reassure me and say they don't notice anything, my huge, crooked nose and uneven skin just look so obvious and terrible to me that I stay convinced the flaws are real.
Have you ever thought that other people might be seeing your appearance differently than you do, or do you believe with complete certainty that the flaw is real and obvious to everyone?

Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers constantly tell me I look fine and that they don't notice anything wrong, I still feel completely convinced that the flaws are real. It is just very hard to believe them because when I look at photos, my huge, crooked nose and uneven skin are glaringly obvious and they are all I can see.
Do you think other people can see the same flaw in your appearance that you see, or do you think they are mistaken and the flaw is definitely real even if no one else notices it?

I think other people are just being nice or are mistaken when they say they don't notice anything. To me, my crooked nose and uneven skin feel completely real and obvious, and I can't help but believe they are actually there regardless of what others say.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things others could not, or had other experiences like feeling that people are spying on you, controlling you, or trying to harm you?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I've never felt like anyone was trying to spy on me or harm me.

When you are not looking at photos or mirrors, can you ever recognize that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or possibly not true, or do you stay completely convinced all the time that the defect is real?

I'm not really sure, as it's hard to tell because the worry is always in the back of my mind. Even when I'm not looking at a photo, it still feels very real to me, so I don't really think of it as exaggerated.

Outside of your appearance concerns, have you ever had other fixed beliefs that other people say are not true, such as being specially watched, followed, harmed, or having a message or special meaning meant just for you?

No, I have never experienced anything like that or had those kinds of beliefs. I've never felt like I was being followed, watched, or that there were special messages meant for me. My worries are strictly about my appearance and how bad I look in photos.
Outside of your appearance concerns, have you ever had other fixed beliefs that others say are not true, such as being watched, followed, harmed, or receiving special messages meant just for you?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never felt watched, followed, or like there were special messages meant for me. My concerns are really just about how I look in photos.

When you are not looking in the mirror or at photos, can you ever consider that your appearance concern might be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain all the time that the flaw is real?

It feels completely real to me all the time, so I stay absolutely certain that my nose is huge and crooked and my skin is uneven. Even though my mom, roommate, and coworkers tell me I look fine, it is just so hard to believe anyone else. When I look at myself, those flaws are all I can see, making it feel one hundred percent true.

When you are not looking in a mirror or photo, can you ever think there is a chance your appearance concern might be exaggerated or not actually true, or are you completely certain all the time that the flaw is real?
I'm really not sure, because it's hard to say. Even when I'm not looking at a photo or a mirror, the worry is always in the back of my mind and it feels very real to me.

How much time each day do you spend thinking about, checking, or trying to hide the parts of your appearance that worry you? Does it take more than an hour a day or keep you from doing normal activities?

It definitely takes up several hours every single day, between zooming in on photos to pick apart my nose and skin, taking dozens of selfies, and constantly redoing my makeup and outfits. This has made me late to meetings, and I've even started turning down presentation opportunities and avoiding community events just to stay off camera.

When you think about your appearance concerns, do you ever recognize that they might be unreasonable or exaggerated, even a little, or are you completely convinced they are true despite what others say?

I am completely convinced that the flaws are real. When I look at photos, my crooked nose and uneven skin look so obvious and terrible to me that I just can't see it any other way, even though my family and coworkers try to reassure me that I look fine.

No, I have never had any experiences like that, and I've never felt watched, followed, controlled, or received special messages. My concerns are strictly focused on my physical appearance and how bad I look.

Outside of looking at photos or mirrors, do you ever realize that your concern about your nose or skin might be exaggerated, or are you completely certain it is a real defect even when you are not checking?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it that way, but the worry just feels so real and distressing to me most of the time that it's hard to tell if it's objectively exaggerated.

I'm not really sure about that. It just feels completely real to me when I look at myself, even if everyone else disagrees.

I'm not really sure. It feels completely real to me, so I haven't really thought about whether it could be exaggerated or not.
